summary: A civil war framed as a class war, fought across a federation with trains carrying aid and troops, in a country whose own sayings echo Russia.

points.game: The Federated Cities were caught in “a class war between the New Federation's Resonator and non-Resonator populations”, escalating into a large-scale civil war.
points.real: The two largest combatants were the Red Army, fighting for the establishment of a Bolshevik-led socialist state headed by Vladimir Lenin, and the forces known as the White movement.

points.game: The Resonator front “distributed emergency aid and reinforcements by train” from the Federated Cities to regions such as the Fifth Sector.
points.real: The most intensive use of armoured trains was during the Russian Civil War (1918–1920).

points.game: A New Federation saying, quoted as from the “Old Federation”: “Solaris is the cradle of humanity, but one cannot live in a cradle forever.”
points.real: In a letter written in 1911 he [Tsiolkovsky] indicated his belief that, “Earth is the cradle of humanity, but one cannot live in a cradle forever.”

against: The Bolsheviks won and built a socialist state; the New Federation's winners built a capitalist, corporate one.
The sides are Resonators and ordinary people, not political camps.

summary: A civil war inside a federation, fought with railroads, remembered through soldiers' identity tags, after which the winners built an industrial, corporate economy in a country the wiki already links to America.

points.game: A large-scale civil war across the New Federation's Federated Cities, between the Resonator and non-Resonator fronts.
points.real: The American Civil War … was a civil war in the United States between the Union (“the North”) and the Confederacy (“the South”).

points.game: Aid and reinforcements moved between the Federated Cities and the Fifth Sector by train, with squads deployed en route.
points.real: Railroads, the electrical telegraph, steamships, the ironclad warship, and mass-produced weapons were widely used.

points.game: Resonator soldiers carried dog tags, and the last one standing carried the tags of the fallen, as Lily did.
points.real: During the American Civil War from 1861 to 1865, some soldiers pinned paper notes with their name and home address to the backs of their coats.

points.game: After the war the New Federation “adopted a capitalist economy, which prioritized corporate interests and technological advancement”; the wiki notes its cyberpunk depiction of America, particularly California.
points.real: These included the Morrill Tariff, land grant colleges, a Homestead Act, a transcontinental railroad, the National Bank Act …

against: The American war was fought over secession and slavery; this one is Resonators against ordinary people.
In America the side that lost was not turned into a persecuted minority the way Resonators were.

summary: The “Old Federation” is only mentioned once, but what surrounds it points east: a Tsiolkovsky saying, a federation that calls itself a union, and Soviet space references nearby.

points.game: The “Old Federation” saying is Tsiolkovsky's famous line with Earth swapped for Solaris; the wiki itself says this suggests connections to Russia and the Soviet Union.
points.real: In a letter written in 1911 he indicated his belief that, “Earth is the cradle of humanity, but one cannot live in a cradle forever.”

points.game: The New Federation's Japanese name is ネオユニオン, “Neo Union”.
points.real: A diverse multinational state, it was organized as a federal union of national republics.

points.game: Nearby Soviet space nods: Mornye's name may come from the Molniya satellites, and the Spacetrek Collective's logo resembles the Soyuz cosmonaut patches.
points.real: The Soviet Union, officially the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), was a transcontinental country that spanned much of Eurasia from its formation in 1922 until its dissolution in 1991.

against: The Old Federation appears in a single line of dialogue; the game hasn't said where or what it is.
Mornye and the Spacetrek Collective belong to Lahai-Roi, not the New Federation.

summary: A lawless desert fringe of outlaw gangs and camps beyond the cities, until the government moves in.

points.game: A dangerous badlands region where Exiles built camps and formed bandit gangs, until the government declared war on them.
points.real: This period includes historical events synonymous with the archetypical Old West or “Wild West” such as violent conflict arising from encroaching settlement into frontier land … vigilantism.

against: Outlaw frontiers are a broad genre; nothing in the game names the Old West directly.

summary: A mercenary group that the government hires by contract, including for black ops.

points.game: The Lawless Zone became a hiring ground where the federal government leases contracts to mercenaries, including illegal black ops such as assassinations; the Ghost Hounds are a multinational mercenary group rooted there.
points.real: A private military company (PMC) … is a privately held company that provides armed combat or security services, military training or consulting, or operational support such as intelligence or logistics.

against: PMCs are a general modern pattern rather than one event.

summary: An Italian-styled religious order that rules the city, judges the “faithless” and bans works it dislikes.

points.game: The Order of the Deep is the ultimate authority in Ragunna; those it deems faithless are sent away on the Pilgrim's Sail, and none have returned.
points.real: The Roman Inquisition … was a system of partisan tribunals developed by the Holy See of the Catholic Church, during the second half of the 16th century.

points.game: Roccia was sent on the Pilgrim's Sail for performing a play the Order had banned.
points.real: The Index Librorum Prohibitorum … was a changing list of publications deemed heretical or contrary to morality … Catholics were forbidden to print or read them.

against: The Order worships a Sentinel and exiles by sea; the Inquisition tried people in courts.

summary: A masked carnival in an Italian-styled sea city, later banned by those in power.

points.game: Ragunna's Carnevale is its grandest celebration, “where the masquerades never end”, lasting seven days.
points.real: The Carnival of Venice … is an annual festival held in Venice, Italy, famous for its elaborate costumes and masks.

points.game: After the second Dark Tide many activities were banned by the Order, and the Carnevale eventually ended altogether.
points.real: However, under the rule of Emperor Francis II, the festival was outlawed entirely in 1797 and the use of masks became strictly forbidden.

against: Venice's ban came from a foreign emperor, Ragunna's from its own religious order.

summary: An Italian-styled banking family whose bank carries a name the Medici claimed as their own.

points.game: Averardo Vault, built by the Montelli Family, is “the leading bank in all of Rinascita”, holding precious metals and artworks and offering secure storage and appraisals.
points.real: Giovanni di Bicci de' Medici established the bank in Florence.

points.game: The vault carries the name “Averardo”.
points.real: He was named after the legendary knight Averardo, from whom the Medici claimed descent.

points.game: As Ragunna opened to the wider world, the Montellis rose to prominence, “amassing great wealth and unmatched influence”.
points.real: It was not until his son Cosimo the Elder took over in 1434 as gran maestro that the Medici became the unofficial head of state of the Florentine Republic.

against: The Medici came to run Florence; the Montelli hold influence but the Order of the Deep rules Ragunna.

summary: A place named after the primordial void of Norse myth, in a region full of Old Norse names.

points.game: Ginnungamere is an area of Mount Gjallar in the Roya Frostlands, where names like Bjartr and Sigrika come from Old Norse.
points.real: In Norse mythology, Ginnungagap (“gaping abyss”, “yawning void”) is the primordial, magical void mentioned in three poems from the Poetic Edda.

against: Only the name matches so far; the area's story isn't known yet.

summary: A yearly night for the dead, with masks and ghost costumes, when lost spirits are said to return.

points.game: An annual festival in Egla Town honouring the deceased; people wear masks or dress as ghosts, and lost spirits with unfulfilled wishes are said to return.
points.real: It was traditionally believed that the souls of the departed wandered the earth until All Saints' Day, and All Hallows' Eve provided one last chance for the dead to gain vengeance.

points.game: Each year has a ghost-themed costume theme, most recently “ghost girl”.
points.real: Popular Halloween activities include trick-or-treating …, attending Halloween costume parties, carving pumpkins …

against: Rinascita is Italian-styled, so an Italian All Souls' tradition may be the closer source.
